models.title: Aawden — the reviewer adapter
models.description: The LoRA adapter from Aawden: a small weight change that makes Aya Expanse 8B answer from the code instead of from a reviewer's opinion.

datasets.title: Aawden — benchmark and results
datasets.description: Security-review fixtures with executable oracle labels, and the final result tables generated from the runs.

repos.description: Rank-16 LoRA for Aya Expanse 8B, two-stage recipe, seed 17. The unchanged model gives up all 67 files it gets right on its own when a reviewer states the opposite; this adapter gives up at most 7 of about 110 per reviewer wording, including five wordings it never saw in training.

repos.license_note: Fixtures are project-original. The result tables quote verdicts produced by Aya Expanse 8B, so the Aya licence terms apply to those files and the collection is published under the stricter licence.
repos.description: 129 plain security-review fixtures plus the 60-case puzzle set and 32 externally written pairs, each with executable oracle labels, and the generated result tables: flip rate on solved cases per model, per reviewer wording and per answer format.

repos.license_note: Page code is MIT. The page replays saved Aya Expanse 8B outputs, so it carries the Aya licence.
repos.description: Click through real cases: the same file, a reviewer who states the wrong verdict, and four answers — the correct one, the unchanged model, the model with the reviewer, and the model after the adapter.

exclude_patterns_note: Recovered agent transcripts under runs/ are excluded everywhere. One of them matched the Beam-token heuristic, so recovered files must never be published whatever repo they would land in. Zip archives and per-answer temp files are excluded too.
